synthetic_data_notice: Every number below comes from synthetic data with no clinical review.

pre_registered_bar.text: At least 5 more minutes of median warning than the plan's baseline at the same alerts per shift.
pre_registered_bar.measure: Median warning over all breaches (a miss counts as zero), the lower end of the 95% paired-bootstrap interval over the 6 held-out runs.
pre_registered_bar.not_assessed_at_1_per_shift: At 1 per shift the plan's baseline catches 46 of 100 and the measures disagree; see the table.

caveats: Synthetic data: the 11967 specimens were written by claude-haiku-5-5 and no clinical review was done (plan task K2 was skipped).
The data and the model share assumptions, because both are ours: the generator's leg times and fault rates are assumed, and the location filter uses the same ones. Read every result as a best case.

The plan's baseline ignores the stability window and the model uses it. The window-aware baseline is the check: at equal weights the model ties it at 4 and 6 alerts per shift (40.0 and 45.0 min median warning over all breaches against 40.0 and 45.0) and trails it at 2 (25.0 against 30.0).

The budget is generous: 6 alerts per shift is about a third of all specimens (18.9 specimens and 0.79 breaches per 8-hour shift on the held-out runs). The knob is set on the fit runs, and the held-out volume at the 6-per-shift setting is 6.4.

The urgency weights move the headline. At 6 alerts per shift the model's median warning over all breaches is 55.0 min at weights 3, 2, 1, 45.0 at equal weights and 50.0 at 9, 3, 1. The extra comes from tiers 1 and 2; tier 3 (61 of the 100 breaches) gets 40.0 min at 3, 2, 1 and 45.0 at equal weights. Every weight is an assumption.
Weak discrimination: the Brier score is only slightly better than the base rate (0.109 against 0.119 at 30 minutes of silence, 0.182 against 0.187 at 60), so the gain is in timing, not in sorting.
33 of 12000 requested specimens were dropped by the validator, and they lean toward long delays (21 of 356 specimens with a stage of 120 minutes or more); see the manifest.

The fit: the pooled stalled weight (5.4% of arrivals) describes the tail and is not the planted stall rate (about 3%), and the body of the distribution before 30 minutes is off by up to 0.028. From 30 minutes on, survival recovers within 3 standard errors.

Location: the most likely place is right 49, 55, 39 and 44 percent of the time at 15, 30, 60 and 90 minutes of silence, against 34, 38, 30 and 39 percent for always naming the commonest place. Only 13 specimens were really lost.

location.note: synthetic data with no clinical review; the filter's structure and fault mix are assumptions the data was drawn with
